invariant: Linguistic stance is evidence about the utterance/speaker stance report; it is not automatically evidence for or against the target proposition.

cases.surface: sha mi ga ran do sava.
cases.interpretation: The speaker reports/marks the proposition as both-sided or contradicted; parsing alone does not fabricate the underlying positive and negative witnesses.

cases.surface: ta mi ga ran do sava.
cases.interpretation: The stance report has a truth-oriented profile. Whether the utterance itself counts as evidence-for the proposition is a separate evidential policy question.

cases.surface: na mi ga ran do sava.
cases.interpretation: The stance report differs from ta despite identical aggregate reading; the Chu profile is preserved.

cases.surface: mu mi ga ran do sava.
cases.interpretation: The grammar can report an unwitnessed/void stance without deleting or overwriting whatever target evidence another subsystem may already hold.
A target proposition becomes stable because both evidence sides are actually populated, independently of whether any utterance used sha.

analogy: SignStuff source-statement resources distinguish evidence that a source asserted a statement from a truth judgment about the statement itself.
nextTest: Project current SignCraft clause readings into stance-report objects while leaving proposition evidence empty; then inject independent evidence and verify the target FOUR reading changes only from evidence.
